messages:
SRE-Bot: :rotating_light: Pager — serving-runtime prefill OOMs detected on cluster gpushare-prod-3 (multiple container restarts). Alert level: P1. paging @Devon Patel oncall.

Devon Patel: Oncall here, picking up. Seeing high restart rate for prefill workers, reproducing locally now. Any immediate customer-facing errors?

CS-Alert: Customer-facing: several Dedicated tenants reporting 502/503 during generation windows. Error spike correlates with 16:45–16:55 UTC.

Erica Chen: I can confirm logs from pod run-serve-prefill-7 show repeated cuda allocations failing. stack: `cudaErrorMemoryAllocation` then container exit code 137.

Mike Torres: Pasting last 50 lines of kube logs from one of the pods:
```
[2026-03-15T16:46:12Z] INFO prefill: starting prefill id=abc123 ctx_bytes=18446744073709551615
[2026-03-15T16:46:12Z] ERROR runtime: cudaErrorMemoryAllocation at device 0
[2026-03-15T16:46:12Z] ERROR runtime: cannot allocate KV cache (requested 12.3GB)
[2026-03-15T16:46:12Z] FATAL runtime: container exiting with status 137
```
Devon Patel: That ctx_bytes looks wrong — `184467...` indicates unsigned wrap / overflow. Might be a bug in context size calculation causing massive allocation attempts.

Erica Chen: Agreed. Likely long system messages + user prompt got counted twice. We should mitigate by rejecting prefill requests > configured max and by patching the allocator guard ASAP.

Julia Nguyen: Immediate mitigation plan: 1) Apply emergency runtime feature-flag `reject_large_prefill=true` via config service to drop prefill requests with computed ctx_bytes > 2e9 (2GB). 2) Route impacted customers to fallback model redwood-medium (smaller KV) for next 30 minutes. 3) Cordon gpushare-prod-3 and evict non-critical pods to reduce noisy neighbors.

Devon Patel: I'm running the feature flag update now. `curl -XPOST https://config.internal/v1/flags -d '{"reject_large_prefill":true}'` 
Devon Patel: Feature flag applied. Confirmed by /admin UI.

Mike Torres: Routing change: updating traffic policy to route model:redwood-xl-prefill -> fallback redwood-medium for Dedicated tenant IDs 235, 412, 789. Pushing canary rule now.

SRE-Bot: Action log: 1802401234 - feature_flag:reject_large_prefill set=true by Devon Patel. route_update initiated by Mike Torres. node_cordon gpushare-prod-3 by Erica Chen.

Erica Chen: Cordoned gpushare-prod-3 (`kubectl cordon gpushare-prod-3a`). Evicting non-critical batch pods.

Mike Torres: Canary routing applied to 10% traffic, monitoring metrics. Errors dropped from 7% -> 2% in canary window.

Devon Patel: Rolling patch to runtime guard now. Small change: check for overflow when computing context_bytes and cap at max_prefill_bytes. Building image `runtime-hotfix:20260315-oom-guard`.

Julia Nguyen: Build passed smoke tests. Deploying to prefill pool in gpushare-prod-3 (canary 2 pods).

Erica Chen: Watch logs on canary:
```
[2026-03-15T16:52:40Z] WARN prefill: request rejected: computed_ctx_bytes=18446744073709551615 > max_prefill_bytes=2147483648
[2026-03-15T16:52:40Z] INFO prefill: rejected request id=def456 reason=ctx_overflow
```

Devon Patel: That's the expected behavior. Rejects are returning 400 with suggestion to truncate prompt. Will add a short error message for SDK teams.

CS-Alert: Notifying impacted customers: sent initial incident email to tenants 235 and 412 — asking them to retry with smaller contexts. Customer Ops tracking ticket: INC-235-2026.

Product-Oncall: Noted that a high-volume enterprise was hit during a nightly batch. They saw ~45 failed requests in a 10-minute window. Asking for a conservative SLA credit calc after postmortem.

Mike Torres: Canary patched pods stable for 8 minutes, error rates in gpushare-prod-3 dropped to baseline. Proceeding to rollout patch to remaining prefill pool with 5-min ramp.

SRE-Bot: Automated step: scaling down prefill concurrency on gpushare-prod-3 by 30% while rollout completes.

Devon Patel: Patch fully rolled out at 16:59 UTC. Node still cordoned; keeping cordon until end of incident.

Erica Chen: Follow-up tasks: open a Jira for root cause analysis — likely integer overflow in context size calculation in the prefill path. Need unit tests for extreme header/system message sizes and guardrails in compile-time checks.

Julia Nguyen: Handoff to night oncall: Julia Nguyen taking post-incident watch until 02:00 UTC. Please monitor for residual restarts, customer callbacks, and verify no regressions from reject path.

Julia Nguyen: Oncall checklist I ran: review logs for `OOM`/`cudaError*`, check restart count on nodes, confirm route fallback removal window (we keep fallback for 30m), ensure playbook steps were followed: https://redwood.internal/playbooks/prefill-oom

Devon Patel: Incident summary for postmortem: root-cause suspected = incorrect unsigned handling of context length -> overflow -> massive allocation request -> GPU OOM -> container restarts. Mitigations applied = runtime guard (reject_large_prefill), traffic routing to smaller model, node cordon, eviction of non-critical pods. Customer impact = multiple Dedicated tenants experienced ~2–7% error spike, one enterprise saw ~45 failed requests.

Product-Oncall: Please prepare a customer-facing timeline and mitigation summary. I'll draft initial message and coordinate with CS-Alert.

CS-Alert: Drafted email sent to affected customers. Will append postmortem link after RCA.

Erica Chen: Leaving a follow-up to engineering: add compile-time caps and safe arithmetic in context size calculations, add integration test with 10MB system messages. Also add realtime metric for `prefill_reject_rate` with reason tag `ctx_overflow`.

Devon Patel: Marking incident as mitigated at 17:04 UTC. We'll keep this thread open for updates. Logging incident in incidents tracker and creating PM for postmortem owner.

SRE-Bot: Incident state updated: mitigated. Incident killer note: next steps assigned to Erica Chen (RCA owner) and Mike Torres (routing/rollback owner).

Julia Nguyen: Taking watch. If anything spikes, page me. Otherwise I'll update status at 02:00 UTC and move to postmortem prep.

Devon Patel: Thanks everyone. Great quick coordination. :thumbsup:
